The Distributed Energy Crisis

The Changing Energy Landscape

Distributed resources like solar, batteries, EV charging, and smart buildings are multiplying rapidly. Yet their value is severely eroded by five structural bottlenecks.

PROBLEM 01

Fragmented Energy Intelligence

Siloed monitoring without holistic visibility

Solar PV, energy storage, EV chargers, HVAC systems, and building automation suites run on isolated proprietary portals with zero joint context.

Impact: Operators miss cross-asset synergies and operate blind to systemic strain.
PROBLEM 02

Unpredictable Demand & Generation

Static setpoints fail under renewable volatility

Solar intermittency and sudden load spikes cause unpredicted tariff penalties, peak demand charges, and costly grid dependency.

Impact: Reactive interventions occur after cost spikes or voltage violations have already happened.
PROBLEM 03

Inefficient Coordination

Isolated optimization creates conflicting incentives

Adjacent facilities on shared feeders export solar simultaneously, depressing export value while creating local grid congestion.

Impact: Clean energy is curtailed while neighboring buildings burn fossil fuels to meet peak demand.
PROBLEM 04

Inadequate Scenario Testing

Operating live assets without safe sandboxes

Asset managers cannot evaluate new dynamic tariffs, extreme weather events, or equipment outages prior to real-world deployment.

Impact: High operational risk and resistance to adopting flexible energy strategies.
PROBLEM 05

Unverified Flexibility

Unsubstantiated claims without auditable proof

Flexibility markets and sustainability auditors lack transparent, verifiable accounting of whether storage dispatch genuinely shifted load or beat baselines.

Impact: Erosion of trust between asset owners, energy aggregators, and regulatory bodies.
The Central Problem Statement

“How can distributed energy resources across multiple facilities be represented, predicted, simulated, optimised and coordinated through an intelligent digital-twin platform, while maintaining operational constraints and independently evaluating the results?”

The Five Pillars of Resolution

The MORQENT Solution

Each capability is built to answer an essential operational question that conventional building management and energy dashboards fail to address.

Anticipate

Predictive Intelligence

“What will our generation, demand, and grid tariffs look like over the next 24 to 72 hours?”

Mechanism:

High-resolution probabilistic forecasting fusing physical asset models, numerical weather data, and occupancy patterns.

Core Deliverable:

Quantified uncertainty bands and multi-horizon demand/generation trajectories.

Schedule

Prescriptive Optimisation

“What is the mathematically optimal schedule for our batteries, EV chargers, and flexible HVAC loads?”

Mechanism:

Constraint-aware Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) solving cost, peak demand, and battery degradation trade-offs.

Core Deliverable:

Feasible setpoints adhering to thermal, electrical, and contractual boundaries.

Evaluate

Scenario Simulation

“What happens if a major transformer fails, a heatwave hits, or dynamic tariff quadruples?”

Mechanism:

High-fidelity digital twin simulation testing contingencies without risking live infrastructure.

Core Deliverable:

Stress-test scorecards and preemptive contingency dispatch strategies.

Harmonise

Coordinated Operation

“How can multiple adjacent facilities avoid competing for local substation headroom?”

Mechanism:

Multi-agent coordination protocol negotiating mutual constraints and shared feeder capacities.

Core Deliverable:

Coordinated multi-site dispatch avoiding collective peak charges and export bottlenecks.

Prove

Verification Ledger

“Did the coordinated optimization actually deliver value over business-as-usual operation?”

Mechanism:

Independent deterministic counterfactual engine comparing actual performance against calibrated persistence baselines.

Core Deliverable:

Tamper-evident flexibility accounting and auditable savings proof.

Specialised Multi-Agent System

Nine Specialised AI Agents

Structured into three disciplined cohorts with centralized orchestration: Sense & Model, Decide, and Prove.

Foundational Agent Design Rule

“Agents orchestrate tools and models; they do not invent numerical operating decisions. Mathematical optimisation produces the schedules, and deterministic safety checks validate them before any action.”

SENSE & MODEL

Asset Modeling Agent

Maintains calibrated physical parameter models of storage, solar, and building envelope thermodynamics.

Primary Inputs:Raw telemetry · Manufacturer nameplate data · Historical degradation curves
Outputs:Calibrated asset model parameters · Health & degradation coefficients
Governance Boundary:Physics-constrained regression & parameter boundary checks
SENSE & MODEL

Forecast Agent

Produces multi-horizon rolling forecasts of solar yield, building demand, and market pricing.

Primary Inputs:NWP weather forecasts · Calendar events · Smart meter telemetry history
Outputs:24h-72h probabilistic forecast distributions with confidence bands
Governance Boundary:Ensemble verification against persistence benchmarks
SENSE & MODEL

State Estimator Agent

Synthesises disparate sensor data into a coherent, noise-filtered snapshot of the full system state.

Primary Inputs:Sub-second meter readings · Inverter state frames · BMS register reads
Outputs:Reconciled state vectors (SoC, voltages, temperatures, power flows)
Governance Boundary:Kalman filtering and physical law conservation checks
DECIDE

Optimization Agent

Formulates and executes the mathematical LP/MILP problem to generate schedule setpoints.

Primary Inputs:State vectors · Forecast vectors · Tariff structures · Physical constraints
Outputs:Optimal 24h asset setpoint vectors (charge/discharge kW, HVAC setpoints)
Governance Boundary:Deterministic mathematical solver with proven convergence criteria
DECIDE

Scenario Simulator Agent

Runs fast-forward 'what-if' simulations across alternative operating conditions and stress scenarios.

Primary Inputs:Candidate schedules · Weather extremes · Equipment outage scenarios
Outputs:Risk profiles, contingency feasibility ratings, resilience scores
Governance Boundary:Isolated digital twin execution sandbox without live actuators
DECIDE

Coordination Agent

Harmonises dispatch schedules across adjacent facilities sharing distribution constraints.

Primary Inputs:Individual facility schedules · Shared substation headroom · Grid tariffs
Outputs:Coordinated cross-site setpoints preventing coincident grid peaks
Governance Boundary:Consensus protocol with strict privacy-preserving data exchange
PROVE

Constraint Safety Agent

Performs deterministic, non-negotiable safety validation on every candidate schedule prior to dispatch.

Primary Inputs:Candidate dispatch vectors · Hard thermal/voltage limits · Battery warranties
Outputs:Binary safety certification or rejection with constraint violation cause
Governance Boundary:Zero-tolerance deterministic rules engine (never overridden by ML)
PROVE

Verification Agent

Quantifies actual financial, energetic, and carbon outcomes against verified counterfactual baselines.

Primary Inputs:Executed power profiles · Calibrated baseline models · Actual tariff rates
Outputs:Auditable performance certificates, verified peak-shaving magnitude
Governance Boundary:IPMVP standard counterfactual comparison framework
PROVE

Continuous Learning Agent

Monitors forecast residuals and optimization gaps to update twin parameters for future cycles.

Primary Inputs:Forecast errors · Model discrepancies · Post-dispatch verification data
Outputs:Parameter fine-tuning weights and model retraining triggers
Governance Boundary:Bounded adaptive learning with rollback safeguards

Scientific Rigour & Benchmarking

Validation & Experiments A–D

We hold ourselves to strict scientific accountability. MORQENT evaluates four comparative control regimes under identical synthetic conditions.

The Honest Hypothesis

“The study tests whether D adds measurable value over C. No results are claimed, and a null result will be reported as such.”

Experiment RegimeForecast InformedMath OptimisationCross-Facility CoordAgent OrchestrationIndependent Verification
AConventional Baseline
Standard timer-based rules and reactive threshold controllers operating independently at each site.
BIndependent Optimisation
Individual sites run local LP/MILP optimization without awareness of neighbors or shared substation headroom.
CCentralised Monolithic Optimisation
A single monolithic solver solves all facilities simultaneously with shared constraints.
DMORQENT Multi-Agent Coordination
Hierarchical agent architecture orchestrating local mathematical optimization with multi-site coordination and independent verification.

Five Non-Negotiable Acceptance Criteria

Zero Hard-Constraint Violations

100% adherence to thermal, voltage, battery SoC bounds, and occupant comfort limits under all operational states.

Forecasts Beat Persistence Baselines

Predictive engine consistently out-predicts standard naive and persistence baselines across all horizons.

Reproducibility & Open Benchmarking

Simulation workflows, synthetic datasets, and verification scripts are fully deterministic and re-runnable.

Fair Comparison Environment

Identical facility models, weather series, and tariff rates are applied uniformly across Experiments A, B, C, and D.

Traceable & Auditable Verification

Every flexibility dispatch and reported saving is cryptographically tied to raw telemetry and deterministic math.

Safety & Trust Kernel

Responsible AI & Industrial Security

Energy infrastructure demands zero hallucinations and non-negotiable physical guarantees. Autonomy is earned through transparency and deterministic safety checks.

PILLAR 01

Human-Supervised Decisions

Always under operator authority

The platform operates with an explicit human-in-the-loop gate ('Authorise'). High-impact schedules require affirmative supervisor approval before actuation.

PILLAR 02

Constraint Validation

Physics and safety are non-negotiable

Every candidate dispatch is validated against strict deterministic physical, thermal, and voltage bounds. Machine learning never overrides physical laws.

PILLAR 03

Complete Auditability

Immutable operational provenance

All telemetry, forecasts, optimization formulations, operator authorizations, and dispatch setpoints are logged in an immutable, cryptographically signed ledger.

PILLAR 04

Industrial Cybersecurity

Zero-trust edge-to-cloud fabric

End-to-end TLS 1.3 encryption, role-based access control (RBAC), segregated OT/IT network proxies, and air-gap compatible local fallbacks.

PILLAR 05

Progressive Autonomy

Earned trust over verified milestones

Facilities advance through structured autonomy tiers: Shadow Simulation → Advisory Recommendations → Supervised Control → Fully Autonomous Closed Loop.

Key Risks & Technical Mitigations

Honest engineering acknowledges constraints upfront. Here is how MORQENT addresses real-world operational failure modes.

Operational Risk 01

Telemetry Latency & Missing Sensor Data

Engineered Mitigation

State Estimator Agent deploys Kalman filtering, physical conservation laws, and robust fallback persistence models to bridge gaps gracefully.

Operational Risk 02

Optimization Solver Timeout on Complex Networks

Engineered Mitigation

Hierarchical decomposition: individual facilities solve localized MILP in parallel; central coordinator negotiates boundary adjustments only.

Operational Risk 03

Equipment Warranty Invalidation

Engineered Mitigation

OEM operating constraints, cycle depth limits, and thermal boundaries are hard-coded as non-violable constraints in the optimization matrix.

Operational Risk 04

Operator Distrust & Resistance to Autonomy

Engineered Mitigation

Progressive autonomy staging starting in passive shadow mode, with plain-language explanation of why schedules were chosen and 1-click override.

Operational Risk 05

Regulatory Barriers in Local Electricity Markets

Engineered Mitigation

Platform delivers immediate internal behind-the-meter savings (peak shaving, self-consumption) regardless of external market readiness.

Operational Risk 06

Cybersecurity Vulnerability in Actuation Links

Engineered Mitigation

Segregated unidirectional data diodes, command whitelisting, rate-limiting on setpoint adjustments, and hardware-level interlocks.
